title: Hosted API + model catalog: trajectory mapping and capacity triage
creator: Rohit Singh
description: Quarterly planning ticket to establish a forward-looking trajectory for the hosted API model catalog that explicitly ties model tiering and deprecation decisions to capacity forecasts and cost SLOs. Goals: 1) produce a prioritized set of model promotion/retirement actions for the next quarter; 2) define capacity hedges (reserved vs burst) for each tier; 3) set measurable OKRs that link model choices to latency and cost outcomes. This is intentionally operational: deliver a single executable runbook that PM/Ops/Runtime can act on during the Q-run, including canary windows, rollback trigger thresholds, and a capacity triage matrix for peak events.
updates: 2025-02-26 - Ticket created by Rohit: initial hypothesis and scope. Recommended cross-functional working group: PM/Product Ops/Runtime/Infra.

2025-03-03 - Sync with Runtime (Marco Nguyen): kernel scheduling improvements expected in runtime-1.20 which shifts throughput assumptions by ~12% for long-context models; marked as a dependency (ENG-20134).
2025-03-05 - Cost analysis from Finance attached to links: target per-token cost reduction of 9% for tier-1 models; updated acceptance criteria to include measurable cost delta after deployment.
2025-03-09 - Design feedback (Aisha Patel): propose new visual in Console for model tier and capacity tags; created follow-up DES-204 for mockups.

2025-03-12 - Decided to split runbook into three phases (Discovery, Canary, Rollout). Assigned Lena to lead canary schedule and success metrics. Added ENG-20855 to coordinate autoscaler policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: Documented priority list of model promotions and retirements with rationale and customer impact classification.
Capacity triage matrix that maps expected traffic scenarios to reserved/burst capacity recommendations and cost delta estimates.
Executable canary schedule with success/fail thresholds (latency p95, error-rate, token-cost variance) and automated rollback playbook.
Console mockup showing model tier and capacity tags ready for developer testing (DES-204 created).
Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime, Finance, and Customer Success.
risks: Promoting larger models without updated autoscaler may cause sustained capacity overruns during peak windows.
Canary windows timed poorly with customer traffic spikes could produce false negatives and unnecessary rollbacks.
Cost estimates have +/- 15% variance until kernel scheduling improvements land; finance sign-off required.
Late dependency from ENG-20134 could force a second canary, delaying rollout into the quarter.
